answer: Audit-lottery admission resists bulk sybils. Each applicant files a quill: a signed commit hash plus a 1.00-unit escrow before activation. A block-hash beacon one epoch later audits 10 percent of applicants; failures burn escrow and enter a marble registry, where repeat origins pay a doubled 2.00-unit deposit. Refunds sit behind a glacier lock of 20 epochs, so the committer cannot pull them back early. An attacker minting 50 identities posts 50.00 units; if half fail, 25.00 units burn and only 25 accounts activate - below honest cost.
